terms.gloss: an orphan boy; a ward under a guardian
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.37: ā pūpillō Hejō, cui C. Mārcellus tūtor est (Lewis & Short) s.v. tūtor

terms.gloss: orphaned, fatherless; also bereaved of a child, childless
terms.grammar: adjective, with the ablative or genitive of the one lost
evidence: Ter. Ph. 125: ut orbae quī sunt genere proximī eīs nūbant
Cic. Q. Fr. 1.3.10: fīliī meī, tē incolumī, orbī nōn erunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In Athenian comedy the orba is the fatherless girl whom the law gives in marriage to her nearest kinsman.

phrases.latin: ā pūpillō Hejō, cui C. Mārcellus tūtor est
phrases.english: from the orphan Heius, whose guardian is Gaius Marcellus

phrases.latin: Lēx est, ut orbae quī sunt genere proximī eīs nūbant.
phrases.english: There is a law that orphan girls shall marry their nearest kinsmen.

sources: Lewis & Short: pupillus · Lewis & Short: orbus
